dedupe_keys.name: history of on orbit satellite fragmentations 16th edition nasa orbital debris program office 2022 catalogue of 268 satellite breakups and 87 anomalous events

description: The History of On-orbit Satellite Fragmentations is the reference catalogue of satellite breakups kept by NASA's Orbital Debris Program Office at Johnson Space Center. The 16th edition, read on 2026-09-28 through the NASA Technical Reports Server, has an information cut-off of 1 May 2022 and counts 268 fragmentations and 87 anomalous events since 1961, including 26 breakups and 9 anomalous events new since the 2018 edition. Each breakup gets a two-page summary with the object name, international designator, catalogue number, orbit, cause assessment and debris count, and the introduction gives tables of the catalogued population by source country and object type, noting that breakup debris makes up 47 percent of 25,437 catalogued objects in orbit. Coverage is global, from the first breakup in 1961 to May 2022. Access is free: NTRS marks it as public use permitted. Caveats: it is a 716-page PDF, so the event list must be extracted, causes remain unknown for about 30 percent of breakups, and debris counts change as cataloguing continues. It supports space infrastructure risk studies, such as estimating fragmentation rates and the collision hazard to navigation or communication satellites at a given altitude. Related records: the CelesTrak satellite catalogue, ESA's space environment report and NASA's LEGEND debris model.
